rationale: MIN has home field and despite a 7-3 record with some inconsistency, ATL is 3-7 and was shut out by Tampa Bay recently; Minnesota should handle business at home.
BAL has lost four straight and looks like a team in freefall, while HOU is at home and coming off a dominant win over IND; Houston should take advantage of Baltimore's struggles.
TB demolished CAR 43-13 earlier this season and has home field advantage, though CAR has been more consistent lately; Tampa's home edge and head-to-head dominance gives them a slight lean.
Both 8-2 teams are playing elite football, but DET has home field advantage in a division rivalry and has been winning close games consistently, making this a slight lean toward the Lions.
DEN is 8-2 and riding a four-game winning streak including a win over KC, while PIT has lost two straight; Denver's overall form and talent edge them out on the road.

LA has won four straight with dominant defensive performances while GB is 2-2 in recent games and dealing with multiple offensive line injuries; LA's home field and momentum favor them despite interior OL concerns.
BUF at 9-1 has been dominant all season with blowout wins including over KC's conference rivals, while KC lost to Denver recently; Buffalo's home field and overall form make them the clear lean.
CLE has home field and a better record, and while both teams have been inconsistent, LV is 4-7 and coming off a blowout loss to Denver; Cleveland's home advantage tips the scale.
LAC is 1-9 and one of the worst teams in the league, while NE at 5-5 is a middling team that should be able to handle a rebuilding Chargers squad on the road.
CIN is 7-3 and has won three straight dominant games, while NO is 3-7 and struggling offensively; Cincinnati at home is a strong play here.
NYG at 6-3 has been one of the better teams in the NFC and IND at 3-8 has been poor all season including a 42-7 blowout loss to JAX recently; Giants should win this comfortably.
Both teams are struggling but MIA is 1-9 and has lost nine straight, while NYJ just got a win over LAC; in a battle of bad teams, NYJ's slight edge in recent form gives them the nod.
DAL already beat PHI 38-21 earlier this season, PHI is 3-7 and struggling, and DAL has home field in a division game where they've shown they can put up big numbers.
SF is 9-1 and dominant at home in the division, coming off a 35-10 blowout of MIN; SEA is solid but SF's home field and overall talent edge make them the clear favorite in this NFC West rivalry.
TEN is 1-9 and has lost nine straight including a 40-23 loss to JAX just recently; Jacksonville at home in a division game is as close to a lock as it gets this week.
WAS has won three of their last four including a win over CIN, while ARI is 3-8 and was blown out by LA and KC recently; Washington should handle Arizona on the road.
